claim.title: Wasserstein Stability of Bayes Gap
claim.statement: Under input-distribution shift, the change in the Bayes Gap between the source (pretraining) and target (inference) domains is bounded by a constant times the Wasserstein distance between the prompt distributions, while the Posterior Variance remains intrinsic to the target domain and is not directly penalized by the shift in the same manner.
claim.test_plan: Pretrain a model on a source distribution P_X. Evaluate the Bayes Gap on the source domain and on a shifted target domain Q_X (e.g., shifted mean or variance of inputs). Compute the Wasserstein distance W_1 between the prompt distributions. Verify that the difference in Bayes Gaps is proportional to the Wasserstein distance. Verify that the Posterior Variance term (estimated via posterior variance) does not exhibit the same linear dependence on the shift magnitude as the Bayes Gap.
claim.success_criterion: The correlation between the Wasserstein distance and the change in Bayes Gap is greater than 0.9, while the change in Posterior Variance is significantly smaller or uncorrelated with the shift magnitude.
